claims.text: This paper introduces BrowseComp, a benchmark comprising 1,266 questions requiring persistent web navigation to find hard-to-find, entangled information.
The benchmark is designed to measure core browsing capabilities through short, easily verifiable answers.

Despite sidestepping challenges like generating long answers or resolving ambiguity, BrowseComp effectively exercises persistence and creativity in information finding, analogous to programming competitions for coding agents.
Addressing the English-centric limitation of existing benchmarks, BrowseComp-ZH evaluates LLM agents on the Chinese web with 289 multi-hop questions across 11 domains.

Using a two-stage quality control protocol, the benchmark achieves high difficulty: most models score below 10% accuracy, and even the best-performing system (OpenAI's DeepResearch) reaches only 42.9%.
The benchmark reveals that success requires effective retrieval strategies, sophisticated reasoning, and information reconciliation—capabilities current models still struggle to master.
WebWalkerQA assesses LLMs' ability to systematically traverse website subpages to extract high-quality data, addressing limitations of traditional search engines that retrieve shallow content.
The accompanying WebWalker framework employs a multi-agent explore-critic paradigm mimicking human-like web navigation.
Experimental results demonstrate both the challenge of the benchmark and the effectiveness of combining retrieval-augmented generation with structured web traversal.
This work presents the first comprehensive benchmark specifically for Deep Research Agents, consisting of 100 PhD-level research tasks across 22 fields.

The authors propose two novel evaluation methodologies: a reference-based method with adaptive criteria for assessing research report quality, and a framework evaluating information retrieval capabilities through effective citation count and accuracy.
This benchmark addresses the critical gap in systematically evaluating agents that transform online information into analyst-grade, citation-rich reports.
Search-R1 extends reinforcement learning frameworks to teach LLMs autonomous search query generation during step-by-step reasoning with real-time retrieval.
The approach optimizes reasoning trajectories with multi-turn search interactions, employing retrieved token masking for stable training and an outcome-based reward function.

Experiments on seven question-answering datasets show 41% improvement (Qwen2.5-7B) and 20% improvement (Qwen2.5-3B) over various RAG baselines, providing empirical insights into RL optimization, LLM choices, and response length dynamics in retrieval-augmented reasoning.
WebThinker addresses the limitation of large reasoning models' reliance on static internal knowledge by integrating a Deep Web Explorer module for dynamic web information extraction.
The framework employs an Autonomous Think-Search-and-Draft strategy, seamlessly interleaving reasoning, information gathering, and report writing.
An RL-based training strategy via iterative online Direct Preference Optimization enhances tool utilization.

Experiments on complex reasoning benchmarks (GPQA, GAIA, WebWalkerQA, HLE) and scientific report generation tasks (Glaive) demonstrate significant outperformance over existing methods and strong proprietary systems.

Addressing the success of proprietary systems like DeepResearch on complex benchmarks, WebSailor introduces a post-training methodology instilling the capability to systematically reduce extreme uncertainty in vast information landscapes.

The approach generates novel high-uncertainty tasks through structured sampling and information obfuscation, RFT cold start, and Duplicating Sampling Policy Optimization (DUPO) for agentic RL training.
WebSailor significantly outperforms all open-source agents in complex information-seeking tasks, matching proprietary agents' performance and closing the capability gap.

WebDancer presents a cohesive four-stage paradigm for building end-to-end agentic information seeking agents: (1) browsing data construction, (2) trajectory sampling, (3) supervised fine-tuning for effective cold start, and (4) reinforcement learning for enhanced generalization.
Instantiated on the ReAct framework, WebDancer achieves considerable results on GAIA and WebWalkerQA benchmarks.
The work provides actionable, systematic pathways for developing more capable agentic models through a data-centric and training-stage perspective.
Addressing the scarcity of high-quality training data for information-seeking agents, WebShaper proposes a formalization-driven data synthesis framework using set theory.
The central concept of Knowledge Projections enables precise control over reasoning structure through KP operation compositions.
Starting from seed tasks, a multi-step expansion process uses an agentic Expander with retrieval and validation tools.
Models trained on the synthesized dataset achieve state-of-the-art performance among open-sourced IS agents on GAIA and WebWalkerQA benchmarks.

WebResearcher reformulates deep research as a Markov Decision Process, where agents periodically consolidate findings into evolving reports while maintaining focused workspaces, overcoming context suffocation and noise contamination in mono-contextual approaches.
The framework includes WebFrontier, a scalable data synthesis engine generating high-quality training data through tool-augmented complexity escalation.
The paradigm naturally scales through parallel thinking for concurrent multi-agent exploration.
Extensive experiments across six challenging benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art performance, surpassing frontier proprietary systems.
